recipes.name: Waikiki-Style Meatballs
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can pineapple chunks, juice reserved

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Mix together ground beef, bread crumbs, onion, milk, egg, and salt in a large bowl until well combined. Roll mixture into balls and arrange onto a baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until meatballs are browned on the bottom, about 25 minutes. Transfer to a slow cooker.

Stir together brown sugar and cornstarch in a medium saucepan and place over low heat. Add reserved pineapple juice and vinegar; stir until smooth. Bring to a boil for 1 full minute before removing from heat; pour over meatballs in the slow cooker.
Add pineapple chunks and green bell pepper to the slow cooker.
Cook on Low until flavors are thoroughly combined, 3 to 4 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Waikiki-Style Meatballs
raw_recipe.description: These sweet and sour Waikiki-style meatballs cooked with pineapple and vinegar are great as a main dish served with rice or as a party appetizer.

review.reviewBody: I've been making Waikiki Meatballs for years. The recipe was originally published in a Betty Crocker cookbook in the 1970's, and has always been a family favorite recipe. Make exactly as printed - it's perfect!

Excellent! I followed the directions closely. I made mine in a deep frying pan because I like meatballs to be browned. Made the sauce in a separate pan and then poured it over the meatballs. Cooked it with the cover on the pan. I also added 1/4 tsp. powdered ginger to the meatballs and about 1 T. soy sauce to the brown sugar and corn starch sauce. I made some brown rice to go with this and served it as an entrée. I also used part red wine vinegar and part apple cider vinegar. I added the juice from a 15 ounce can of pineapple chunks. I did not think it was too sweet. I thought it was perfect. Next time I make this I will serve it with steamed broccoli, and some chinese vegetables. And I may toss in some green onion slices. I really enjoyed it. I'm looking forward to eating the leftovers.

Tasted great!!! Doubled the recipe and added 1 tsp garlic powder.
Cooked the meatballs on a pellet smoker with hickory pellets for 1 hour at 275°. Everything else was done as written. Even though the type of vinegar is not specified, my choice is rice vinegar. But between the choices of white or apple cider vinegar, I would use white since it adds to the sweet and sour taste of the sauce.

Made it as written the first time which was very good, then I made a few changes for my seconded time. Used 2 lbs. ground beef 1 lb. pork sausage & added a pinch of Chinese 5-spice 2 garlic cloves minced. For the sauce I used a whole red & green bell peppers, red onion & 2 stalks of celery all chopped and sautéed . Made it a bit better.
Thanks

I made it with 50% lean ground beef and 50% ground Peppered Bacon. I baked the meat balls on the treager at 300 degrees for 30 minutes while I made the sauce then simmered the meatballs for 30 min. Served over jasmine rice. Yummy

I have loved this recipe for years. Never thought about putting it in the crock pot, but it works for soccer practice night :) the original recipe calls for 1/4 teaspoon ginger for the meat balls and 1 tablespoon soy sauce for the sauce. I highly recommend adding that to what is written here.
My family has been enjoying this dish for over 30 years but we add a 1/2 tsp of ginger to the meatballs and in the sauce as well. Family favorite!

Good recipe if it is an appetizer. If you want to serve it as a main course, (served over rice) I'd make a few alterations. I added a small amount of low-sodium soy, then grated in some fresh ginger, some garlic, and some sesame seeds. I had a bottle of Asian sweet/sour sauce in the frig that I added in as well. My slow cooker is the kind that you can brown and saute in as well, so I browned the meatballs, then added the sauce called for in the recipe, then the green peppers and pineapple, but it was obvious there would not be enough sauce to put over rice, and I thought it could be enhanced with the additional Asian ingredients. Worked out well.
Added 1 tbsp low sodium soy sauce to sauce and 1/2 tsp ground ginger to meatballs. Delish!!!!

I've made these for years. I use not only the pineapple juice but the cherry juice as well. We like a lot of sauce with the meatballs and rice. I like to make a thicker sauce as well and put a bit more cornstarch in. I also add canned lychees if I can find them.

*DROOL* 
These were AMAZING. I used two 1.5 lb bags of frozen meatballs, doubled the measurements for all other ingredients, and set the slow cooker for 4 hours on high. I'm sure fresh meatballs can be cooked on low but I wanted to play it safe since I was using frozen and they were absolutely perfect.
These were a hit as appetizers. I used ready made, frozen, all beef meatballs, added a bit of ginger and soy sauce to the pineapple sauce, and simmered everything in the crockpot on low for 4 hours.

I have been making this very same recipe for over 40 years. It was received in a cookbook from military wives that was a wedding present. I also now use plain frozen meatballs and often add red, yellow, or orange sweet peppers for additional color. I also add either chives or finely sliced green (spring) onions when serving. It makes great leftovers.
Excellent!

Very good! Hubby and I enjoyed it over white rice, and thought that browning the meatballs before adding them to the sauce added lots of flavor. Will keep fixing this for sure! It keeps very well in the fridge and seems to improve in flavor the 2nd and 3rd days.

IT was really good, family loved it. Meatballs could have had more spices but I guess I could have always added in. Also recipe could have stated better maybe as to what size to make the meatballs --apps or entree and larger ones I think would affect the cooking time. but very tasty all in all and kinda easy

Thanks for posting! This recipe is a classic and I remember making these back in the 70's. I like to saute the pineapples so they start to brown before adding them to the sauce. The recipe is a great balance of sweet and sour and with pre-made frozen meatballs, preparation is quick and easy.
thank you

It's obvious that this recipe was from the 70's. No taste worth bragging about . I am going to make again and update the recipe. This was probably really good to people back in the 70's when cooking and spices weren't a big thing like today. Sorry Betty Crocker!!
Tryrrrrrrr
